headline: Simulation and neural surrogates recover interpretable dynamics in biological systems
label: Simulation Driven Biological Dynamics Modeling
summary: Neural and symbolic inference methods increasingly recover parameters and reduced dynamics from simulated biological time series.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of simulation as both a generative testbed and a source of inferential leverage for biological dynamical systems. Simulation-based reverse engineering of a simplified layer 5 cortical model attributes enhanced information flux in a dense core to an embedding network. Limit cycles coupled to reaction-diffusion models are reported to sweep Turing-permissive regimes, aiding detection of rare patterns. Physics-informed neural networks are evaluated for recovering repressilator ODE parameters under noise and sparse sampling, while Edwin pairs maximum entropy dimensionality reduction with sparse symbolic model discovery to infer interpretable low-dimensional dynamics. The most specific new contribution is a systematic examination of how size, diversity and noise of ODE-simulated training data govern transfer learning for biological time-series prediction. Developmental self-organisation studies jointly train neural cellular automata with SIREN pre-patterns.
